mainTopic: What a ממאנת, a שניה and an איילונית lose when they leave a marriage: the dispute about the כתובה, worn-out property, and the basic כתובה versus the תוספת
overview: This amud finishes שמואל's list of differences between a girl who leaves her marriage by מיאון and one who leaves with a גט. The גמרא explains that his real new point is the three-month wait. Next it asks whether רב and שמואל, who argue about whether a ממאנת gets a כתובה, are repeating the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. It concludes that both follow רבי יהושע and only read him differently. Then the גמרא turns to worn-out property (בלאות). שמואל's split between נכסי מלוג and נכסי צאן ברזל fits only the שניה, where the חכמים penalized both spouses. From this, רב שימי בר אשי learns that a cloak a wife brings is principal, and רב נחמן disagrees. Finally, שמואל teaches that 'no כתובה' means only the basic 100 or 200, not the תוספת, and a ברייתא confirms it. The ברייתא's last line supports רב הונא, whose statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A divorced minor must wait three months
steps.stepSummary: This is the last line of שמואל's list. A girl who leaves her marriage with a גט must wait three months before she remarries.
steps.simpleTranslation: A girl who leaves through a גט must wait three months before remarrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing שמואל's list of differences between a girl who refuses (ממאנת) and a girl who gets a גט. This last difference is about waiting three months before marrying again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the list, שמואל said that a ממאנת does not need to wait. Here he says the opposite about a girl who gets a גט: she must wait three months. A גט ends a full marriage, so it brings this extra requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who leaves her marriage through a bill of divorce
To wait three months before remarrying
A minor girl who refuses to stay in her marriage (מיאון), which ends it without a גט

phrases.english: One who leaves through a bill of divorce
is required to wait three months.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹצְאָה בְּגֵט צְרִיכָה לְהַמְתִּין שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes שמואל's list of differences, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A minor who leaves her marriage with a גט must wait three months before remarrying. A ממאנת does not.

steps.title: Why did שמואל need to say this? A משנה already teaches it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל. A משנה in יבמות already lists the differences between a ממאנת and a girl who gets a גט, so what did שמואל add?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned all of it: a girl who refuses her husband: he is permitted to her relatives, she is permitted to his relatives, and she is not disqualified from marrying a כהן. If he gave her a גט: he is forbidden to her relatives, she is forbidden to his relatives, and she is disqualified from marrying a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why שמואל repeated rules that a משנה already teaches. It then quotes that משנה to show the overlap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows that מיאון undoes the marriage, so no family ties are created and she may still marry a כהן. A גט ends a real marriage, so the family prohibitions stay and she becomes a גרושה, who may not marry a כהן. Since this was already known, שמואל's statement looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (asks what new point a statement adds)
We already learned it (in a משנה)
Her female relatives, such as her sister or mother
He disqualified her from marrying a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'he is permitted to her relatives' means that after she leaves, he may marry her relatives. It does not mean anything was allowed during the marriage.

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned all of it:
phrases.notes: The source is a משנה in יבמות (108a).

phrases.english: One who refuses a man —
he is permitted to her relatives,
and she is permitted to his relatives,
and he did not disqualify her from the priesthood.
If he gave her a bill of divorce —
he is forbidden to her relatives,
and she is forbidden to his relatives,
and he disqualified her from the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? תְּנֵינָא כּוּלְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for שמואל's whole list.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's list of differences between a ממאנת and a girl divorced with a גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in יבמות already teaches these differences, so שמואל's statement seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The three-month wait is the new point
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the three-month waiting period is not in the משנה, so שמואל needed to teach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needed to say 'she must wait three months,' because we did not learn that in the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Only one piece of שמואל's list is new: the three-month wait.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה covers relatives and the כהונה, but it never mentions waiting before remarriage. That rule is שמואל's real contribution. The other items were repeated only to complete the list.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him (to say it)
Because we did not learn it in a משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Most of שמואל's list repeats the משנה in יבמות. His new point is that a girl who leaves with a גט must wait three months, and a ממאנת does not.

phrases.english: 'She must wait three months'
he needed to say,
since we did not learn it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies one new point that justifies the whole statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's whole list repeats the משנה in יבמות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The three-month wait is new, and the rest was said only to complete the list.

steps.title: Is this an older dispute between תנאים? רבי אליעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the dispute between רב and שמואל matches a dispute between תנאים. It quotes רבי אליעזר, who holds that a minor's marriage has almost no legal effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is like a dispute between תנאים. רבי אליעזר says: the act of a minor girl is nothing. Her husband has no right to things she finds, to her earnings, or to cancel her vows. He does not inherit her, and he does not become impure for her. The rule is: she is not like his wife in any way, except that she needs מיאון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a comparison. It begins quoting a ברייתא to see whether רב and שמואל are repeating an older dispute between תנאים. This step gives רבי אליעזר's side, and רבי יהושע's view follows in step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that a minor's marriage gives the husband none of a husband's usual rights. He gets no found objects, no earnings, no power to cancel vows, no inheritance, and no permission (as a כהן) to become impure for her burial. The only trace of the marriage is that she must do מיאון to leave it.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this matches a dispute between תנאים?
Lost objects she finds
Her earnings from her work
Canceling her vows
Becomes ritually impure to bury her (allowed for a כהן with a close relative, including his wife)
Refusal; how a minor married by her mother or brothers ends the marriage

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר does not say she is completely unmarried. She still needs מיאון to leave. He only says she has none of a wife's other legal results.

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute of תנאים,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
The act of a minor girl is nothing,
phrases.notes: He means her marriage, when someone other than her father married her off.

phrases.english: and her husband is not entitled to what she finds,
nor to her earnings,
nor to canceling her vows,
and he does not inherit her,
and he does not become impure for her.
phrases.notes: This is about a husband who is a כהן.

phrases.english: The general rule is:
she is not like his wife in any respect,
except that she requires refusal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining שמואל's list to asking whether רב and שמואל repeat an older dispute between תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: a minor's marriage gives her husband none of a husband's rights. It only means she needs מיאון to leave.
steps.raayaObject: The dispute between רב and שמואל about the minor who refuses
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the view of רבי אליעזר (the opposing view of רבי יהושע follows in step 5)

steps.title: רבי יהושע: A minor's marriage counts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע holds that a minor girl's marriage has real legal effect. Her husband gets all the rights of a husband, and she is like his wife in every way, except that she leaves through מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: A minor girl's marriage is something. Her husband gets what she finds and what she earns. He can cancel her vows. He inherits her, and he may become impure for her. The rule is: she is like his wife in every way, except that she leaves through refusal.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the second opinion, רבי יהושע, who argues with רבי אליעזר from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said a minor's marriage is basically nothing. רבי יהושע says the opposite: it gives the husband the full set of husband's rights. The only difference from a regular wife is that she can walk out with מיאון instead of a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: The minor's marriage is 'something': it has legal effect
He inherits from her
She is like his wife in every respect
That she leaves through refusal, not a גט

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
The act of a minor girl is something,
and her husband is entitled to what she finds,
and to her earnings,
and to cancelling her vows,
and he inherits her, and he becomes impure for her.
phrases.notes: Even if he is a כהן, he may become impure to bury her, as he would for any wife.

phrases.english: The general rule is:
she is like his wife in every way,
except that she leaves through refusal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 4 with the opposing תנא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A minor's marriage has legal effect. She is like a wife in every respect except that she leaves through מיאון.

steps.title: Suggesting that רב and שמואל match the two תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that רב, who says a ממאנת gets no כתובה, follows רבי אליעזר, and שמואל, who says she does, follows רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב follows רבי אליעזר, and שמואל follows רבי יהושע?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that both תנאים are quoted, the גמרא spells out its suggestion: line up רב with רבי אליעזר and שמואל with רבי יהושע. This sets up the next move, where the suggestion is tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The match seems natural. If the marriage is nothing (רבי אליעזר), there is no כתובה, like רב. If she is a full wife (רבי יהושע), she should get a כתובה, like שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion that may be rejected.
Marriage contract payment

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav, who said his ruling,
phrases.notes: רב said a girl who leaves through מיאון gets no כתובה, and שמואל said she does.

phrases.english: holds like Rabbi Eliezer,
and Shmuel, who said his ruling, holds like Rabbi Yehoshua?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the two opinions of the ברייתא to propose matching the אמוראים to the תנאים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the רב–שמואל dispute the same as the רבי אליעזר–רבי יהושע dispute?

steps.title: According to רבי אליעזר, everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. According to רבי אליעזר, even שמואל would agree that she gets no כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אליעזר, everyone agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion. It says that if we follow רבי אליעזר, there is no argument at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a minor's marriage is nothing, nobody would give her a כתובה, so שמואל could not be following רבי אליעזר's view. That means the dispute cannot simply be רבי אליעזר against רבי יהושע. It must be somewhere inside רבי יהושע's view.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the opinion of
Everyone agrees, there is no dispute

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Eliezer,
everyone agrees.
phrases.notes: Agrees with רב, that she gets no כתובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the matching proposed in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that שמואל disagrees with רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under רבי אליעזר there is no room for a כתובה, so שמואל would agree with רב.

steps.title: They disagree over how to read רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל both work within רבי יהושע's view. שמואל reads him plainly, so she is a full wife and gets a כתובה. רב says רבי יהושע only gave the husband rights over her, not duties toward her.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they disagree, it is according to רבי יהושע. שמואל follows רבי יהושע plainly. רב says: רבי יהושע only said there that she has duties to him, but he does not have duties to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where the real argument is. Both רב and שמואל accept רבי יהושע, but they read his words differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע said she is 'like his wife in every way.' שמואל takes this fully, so she even gets a כתובה. רב limits it: every example in the ברייתא is a right the husband gets from her, so it does not create money duties from him to her, like a כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said his ruling up to this point, and no further
From hers to his: her duties toward him
From his to hers: his duties toward her

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute is not רבי אליעזר against רבי יהושע. Both רב and שמואל follow רבי יהושע. שמואל says a ממאנת is a full wife and gets a כתובה. רב says רבי יהושע only meant her duties to the husband, so she gets no כתובה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב rejects רבי יהושע. רב accepts him, but limits 'like his wife in every way' to the husband's rights over her.

phrases.english: When they disagree,
it is according to Rabbi Yehoshua:
Shmuel follows Rabbi Yehoshua as he sounds,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָתָם
phrases.english: and Rav says: Rabbi Yehoshua only said it there
from hers to his,
phrases.notes: He means what she owes him, like her finds and earnings, the examples listed in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: but from his to hers, he did not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 7 rejected the matching, this step places the dispute inside רבי יהושע's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the dispute to differing readings of one תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב follows רבי אליעזר and שמואל follows רבי יהושע.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow רבי יהושע. שמואל reads him fully, while רב limits him to her duties toward the husband.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The כתובה dispute depends on whether רבי יהושע's 'like his wife in every way' includes the husband's duties toward her.

steps.title: שמואל limits the rule of no worn-out items to usufruct property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'and not בלאות.' רב הונא בר חייא reports that שמואל limited this to נכסי מלוג. For נכסי צאן ברזל she does get the worn value back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said these women get no worn-out items. רב הונא בר חייא said to רב כהנא: You told us in the name of שמואל that this was taught only about נכסי מלוג. For נכסי צאן ברזל, she does have a claim.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up a new phrase from the משנה, 'ולא בלאות,' and brings שמואל's teaching that narrows it to one type of property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife's property comes in two kinds. נכסי מלוג stay hers, and the husband only eats the profits. With נכסי צאן ברזל, the husband takes responsibility for their value. שמואל says the 'no בלאות' rule only applies to the first kind, so the husband still owes her for worn צאן ברזל.

keyTerms.meaning: Worn-out items, meaning property the wife brought in that wore out during the marriage
Usufruct property: it stays the wife's, and the husband only eats the profits
'Iron sheep' property: the husband takes on responsibility for its full value
'They only taught this about...', a phrase that narrows a rule

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of property. With מלוג the wife keeps ownership. With צאן ברזל the husband carries the risk. That difference drives this whole section.

phrases.english: And not worn-out items.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא לְרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Ḥiyya said to Rav Kahana:
You told us in the name of Shmuel:
They taught this only about usufruct property,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נִכְסֵי צֹאן בַּרְזֶל, אִית לַהּ.
phrases.english: but for guaranteed property, she does have a claim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the כתובה discussion to the next clause of the משנה, about worn-out property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'no בלאות' rule applies only to נכסי מלוג. She does recover worn נכסי צאן ברזל.

steps.title: רב פפא asks which woman שמואל meant
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks which of the three women in the משנה שמואל's distinction refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא thought about it and asked: which case is this about?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא opens a question. He wants to know which woman שמואל was talking about. This sets up the next steps, where the גמרא tests each option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists three women: the ממאנת, the שניה and the איילונית. שמואל's split between the two kinds of property has to make sense for at least one of them. So רב פפא checks each one.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought it over and discussed it
'On which one?', asking which case a statement refers to

phrases.english: Rav Pappa discussed it: to which case does it refer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which case שמואל's statement in step 9 applies to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the three women in the משנה שמואל's distinction refers to.

steps.title: It cannot be about the girl who refuses
steps.stepSummary: If שמואל meant the ממאנת, his split would not work. If the items still exist, she takes both kinds. If they are gone, she takes neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is about the ממאנת: if the items still exist, she takes both this and that. If they no longer exist, she takes neither this nor that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option, the ממאנת, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a ממאנת there is no difference between מלוג and צאן ברזל. Either both come back or neither does. So שמואל's split between them cannot be talking about her.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say...', introducing a suggestion that will be tested
They exist / they no longer exist
This and that, meaning both kinds
She takes

phrases.english: If you say it refers to the girl who refuses,
if the items still exist, she takes both this and that.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי דְּלֵיתַנְהוּ — אִידֵּי וְאִידִי לָא שָׁקְלָא!
phrases.english: And if they no longer exist, she takes neither this nor that!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to רב פפא's question and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects applying שמואל's statement to the ממאנת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For a ממאנת, both kinds of property are treated the same, so a split between them makes no sense.

steps.title: It cannot be about the איילונית either
steps.stepSummary: If שמואל meant the איילונית, his split would come out backwards. If the items are gone, logic would give her the מלוג, which stayed in her possession. It would not give her the צאן ברזל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about the איילונית. But there too: if the items exist, she takes both. If they don't exist, שמואל should have said the opposite. She should get the מלוג, which stays in her possession, and not the צאן ברזל, which is not in her possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second option, the איילונית, and shows that שמואל's rule would be reversed for her. So this option is rejected too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the items still exist, the איילונית gets everything back, so no split. If the items wore out, the reasoning would favor the property that stayed in her possession, the מלוג. That is the opposite of what שמואל said. So his statement cannot be about her.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who cannot have children, whose marriage the משנה treats as having no כתובה
'He should have said the opposite'
They remain in her possession

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to the ailonit:
if the items exist, she takes both this and that;
if they no longer exist, he should have said the opposite:

phrases.aramaic: נִכְסֵי מְלוֹג דְּבִרְשׁוּתַהּ קָיְימִי — אִית לַהּ,
phrases.english: usufruct property, which remains in her possession, she does get,

phrases.aramaic: נִכְסֵי צֹאן בַּרְזֶל דְּלָאו בִּרְשׁוּתַהּ קָיְימִי — לֵית לַהּ!
phrases.english: guaranteed property, which is not in her possession, she does not get!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ממאנת was ruled out, tries the איילונית and rules her out too.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects applying שמואל's statement to the איילונית.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For an איילונית, the reasoning would favor the מלוג over the צאן ברזל, the reverse of שמואל's ruling.

steps.title: It refers to the secondary relative, where both sides are penalized
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's statement is about the שניה. The חכמים penalized both spouses, each in what the other owes. She loses the worn מלוג, and he must pay for the worn צאן ברזל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about the שניה. The חכמים penalized her in what he owes her, and penalized him in what she owes him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer: שמואל was talking about the שניה. His split there comes from a penalty, not from plain logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both husband and wife broke a rabbinic ban by marrying, so the חכמים fined both of them. Her fine is that she gets no payment for the worn מלוג. His fine is that he must still pay her for the worn צאן ברזל. This explains why שמואל gave a different result for each kind of property.

keyTerms.meaning: A relative forbidden to marry by rabbinic law (a 'secondary' relative)
The חכמים imposed a penalty
On her, in what is his to give: she loses what he would owe her

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule (no payment for worn מלוג, but payment for worn צאן ברזל) fits only the שניה. There, the חכמים penalized both spouses, each one in the area where the other would gain.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a rule that seems odd can make sense once we see it is a penalty (קנס) and not the normal rule.

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to the secondary relative,
and the Rabbis penalized her with regard to what is his,
phrases.notes: In plain terms, she loses out on the worn מלוג, which the husband would otherwise have to cover.

phrases.english: and him with regard to what is hers.
phrases.notes: In plain terms, he still has to pay her for the worn צאן ברזל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַשְּׁנִיָּה, וּקְנַסוּ רַבָּנַן לְדִידַהּ בְּדִידֵיהּ וּלְדִידֵיהּ בְּדִידַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the ממאנת and the איילונית, gives the case that works.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the correct case, with a penalty-based reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's split must follow from plain property logic, which fails for the ממאנת and the איילונית.
steps.terutzMaskana: The split applies to the שניה as a rabbinic penalty on both spouses.

steps.title: A wife's cloak is principal, so the husband may not wear it out
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי infers from רב כהנא's statement, now understood as a penalty for the שניה, that a cloak a wife brings counts as קרן (principal). Her husband may not use it until it is worn out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said: We can learn from רב כהנא's statement that if a wife brings her husband a cloak, it counts as principal. He may not keep wearing it until it wears out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי draws a practical rule from the answer we just learned about the שניה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We were just told that losing the worn-out מלוג is a special penalty for the שניה. That means a normal wife does get paid for her worn-out מלוג items. So the husband may not use up her property: a cloak she brings is 'principal' that belongs to her, not 'produce' that he may use up.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this, an inference
A cloak or garment
Principal, the property itself that stays hers
Worn out

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a special penalty (קנס) tells us the normal rule: without the penalty, the wife's מלוג principal is protected.

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi said:
Conclude from the statement of Rav Kahana:
phrases.notes: He means what רב כהנא reported in שמואל's name (step 9). As we just saw, losing the worn-out מלוג there is a penalty for the שניה.

phrases.english: if she brought him a cloak,
it is principal,
phrases.notes: Principal is the item itself, which stays hers. The husband only gets to enjoy the 'produce' of her מלוג.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא מִכַּסֵּי לַהּ וְאָזֵיל עַד דְּבָלֵי.
phrases.english: and he may not keep covering himself with it until it wears out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical rule from the answer given in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cloak a wife brings into the marriage is קרן; the husband may not wear it out.

steps.title: But רב נחמן says using the cloak counts as produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this with רב נחמן's view: wearing the cloak is 'produce,' which the husband may use.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב נחמן say it counts as produce?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב שימי בר אשי's rule with a statement of רב נחמן that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן holds that the use of a garment is like the fruit of a field. So the husband may wear it even if it wears out. That clashes directly with calling the cloak 'principal.'

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [so-and-so] say?, a formula for a challenge
Produce or fruit, the benefit the husband is entitled to

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Nachman say
it is produce!
phrases.notes: Wearing the cloak is treated like eating fruit from her field, which the husband is allowed to do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 14's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שימי בר אשי's rule that the cloak is קרן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן explicitly calls the cloak's use פירא, which the husband may use up.

steps.title: רב נחמן simply holds a different view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב נחמן disagrees. His view is a different opinion, not a problem for the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן's statement disagrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying this is a real disagreement between אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not try to reconcile the two views. It admits that רב נחמן holds the opposite. רב שימי בר אשי's inference from step 14 stands for those who accept רב כהנא's approach.

keyTerms.meaning: Disagrees, a different opinion

phrases.english: Rav Nachman's view is in disagreement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן's statement seemed to disprove the rule that the cloak is קרן.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן simply holds a different opinion; the rule remains according to the other view.

steps.title: Only the basic כתובה is lost, not the extra amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's words 'they have no כתובה.' שמואל says this means only the basic 100 or 200. The תוספת, the extra amount the husband added, is still paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'They have no כתובה.' שמואל said: This was taught only about the basic 100 or 200. But the extra amount, they do get.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new phrase in the משנה and gives שמואל's limit on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic 100 (for a widow) or 200 (for a virgin) was set by the חכמים, so the חכמים can take it away. The תוספת is what the husband chose to add on his own. That part is not covered by 'they have no כתובה.'

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only about, a formula that limits a rule
The basic כתובה: 100 for a widow, 200 for a virgin
The extra amount the husband added to the כתובה

steps.whatToRemember: 'No כתובה' in our משנה means no basic 100 or 200. The תוספת is still owed.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'no כתובה' as 'she gets nothing at all.' Only the basic amount is lost.

phrases.english: "They have no ketubah."
Shmuel said:
They taught this only about the hundred and the two hundred,
but the additional amount, they do have.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לָהֶן כְּתוּבָּה. אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מָנֶה מָאתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting a new phrase from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These women lose the basic מנה/מאתים but still receive the תוספת.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the same as שמואל: women who 'have no כתובה,' like the ממאנת and her companions, lose only the 100 or 200 and still get the תוספת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: Women about whom the חכמים said they have no כתובה, like the ממאנת and her companions, do not get the 100 or 200. But the extra amount, they do get.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up שמואל's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spells out the same split that שמואל made: the basic amount is lost, but the תוספת is kept. So שמואל's limit is confirmed by an earlier source.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way, a supporting ברייתא
A girl who refuses (rejects) a marriage arranged in her childhood
And her companions, the other women in the משנה

phrases.english: It is also taught so in a baraita:
Women about whom the Sages said
they have no ketubah,
such as the one who refuses and her companions,
phrases.notes: The companions are the שניה and the איילונית, the other two women from our משנה.

phrases.english: they do not have the hundred or two hundred,
but the additional amount,
they do have.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's statement in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that only the מנה/מאתים is lost.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says the same split explicitly.

steps.title: The second half of the ברייתא: women who break the rules lose everything
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. Women like the עוברת על דת and her companions get no תוספת, and certainly not the basic 100 or 200. A woman sent away because of a שם רע still takes what is left of her own property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Women about whom the חכמים said that they leave without a כתובה, such as a woman who breaks the rules of Jewish practice and the others listed with her, do not get the תוספת, and certainly not the 100 or 200. A woman sent away because of a bad reputation takes whatever of hers is still there and leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same ברייתא from step 18. Now it describes a stricter group of women who lose everything, and then one more case, the woman with a שם רע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18, a woman like the ממאנת lost only the basic 100 or 200 and kept the תוספת. Here the עוברת על דת is penalized much more heavily: she loses the תוספת too. The phrase כל שכן says that losing the basic 100 or 200 is even more obvious. The last line adds that a woman sent away for a שם רע still keeps what is left of her own property.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who breaks the rules of Jewish law or custom in her marriage
All the more so; even more obviously
A bad reputation, here for improper behavior
Literally 'what is before her': whatever of her own property is still there

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the wording. The ברייתא uses two different phrases. 'אין להן כתובה' (the ממאנת group) means losing only the 100 or 200. 'יוצאות שלא בכתובה' (the עוברת על דת group) means losing everything, the תוספת included.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a clear contrast. Some women lose only the basic כתובה, while women who sinned lose even the extra amount. It also introduces the woman with a שם רע, which the next step uses as support for רב הונא.

phrases.english: Women about whom the Sages said
they leave without a כתובה
for example, a woman who breaks the rules of Jewish practice, and her companions
phrases.notes: 'Her companions' are the other women sent away without a כתובה. They're listed in an earlier משנה in this מסכת, not in our משנה.

phrases.english: do not get the extra amount (תוספת)
and all the more so not the 100 or 200
And a woman who leaves because of a bad reputation
takes what is in front of her and leaves
phrases.notes: He means she takes whatever of her own property is still around when she leaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָשִׁים שֶׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים יוֹצְאוֹת שֶׁלֹּא בִּכְתוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא quoted in step 18 and contrasts the ממאנת group with the stricter עוברת על דת group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עוברת על דת and her companions lose both the תוספת and the basic 100 or 200. A woman divorced for a שם רע takes whatever of her own property remains.

steps.title: The ברייתא supports רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the ברייתא's last line, that a woman with a שם רע takes what is hers, supports רב הונא. רב הונא says a woman who was unfaithful has not lost something. The sentence continues on the next daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רב הונא, because רב הונא said: a woman who was unfaithful has not lost...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא backs up a ruling of רב הונא. It begins quoting him: a woman who was unfaithful still has not lost something of hers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said a woman sent away for a שם רע 'takes what is in front of her,' meaning she keeps her own property. That matches רב הונא's idea that even an unfaithful woman does not lose everything. So the ברייתא serves as a proof for his view.

keyTerms.meaning: It supports him; a source backs up someone's opinion
She was unfaithful
She has not lost

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that being unfaithful does not wipe out a woman's rights to her own property.

phrases.english: This supports רב הונא
as רב הונא said
A woman who was unfaithful has not lost
phrases.notes: The sentence finishes on the next daf, where רב הונא says exactly what she has not lost.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the last line of the ברייתא from step 19, about the woman with a שם רע, as support for רב הונא.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling that a woman who was unfaithful has not lost her rights to her own property.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's line that a woman divorced for a שם רע 'takes what is in front of her and leaves.'
